chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qasani, from Suleiman ibn Hafs al-Marwazi, who said:

I wrote to Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him) regarding the prostration of gratitude, so he wrote to me: 'A hundred times: 'Thank you, thank you,' and if you wish, 'Forgiveness, forgiveness.'
ai.seo_question: What are the recommended words to recite during the Prostration of Gratitude (Sajdat al-Shukr)?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam Musa al-Kadhim (AS), the specific practice of Sajdat al-Shukr is detailed, highlighting the Imam's preference for the concise, potent phrase 'Shukran' (Thank you) recited a hundred times, while offering 'Afwan' (Forgiveness) as a valid alternative. This brevity reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the efficacy of frequent, simple dhikr over lengthy recitations, reinforcing the spiritual discipline of constant gratitude and seeking pardon in daily worship.
